title: Least-Privilege API Security Gateway with RS256 JWT Rotation, Redis Bloom Filter & Device Fingerprinting
problem: Modern cloud-native microservices exposed to public networks face credential theft, token replay attacks, and compromised session hijacking when relying on static API keys or long-lived bearer tokens without instant revocation. Standard API gateways either incur severe latency bottlenecks by performing blocking database queries on every HTTP request or fail to invalidate stolen session tokens across distributed microservices. This project builds a high-performance least-privilege API security gateway in Node.js and Express. The gateway enforces asymmetric RS256 JWT validation with automated JWKS keypair rotation, checks token revocation via an in-memory Redis Bloom filter in sub-millisecond time, verifies cryptographic client device fingerprints, mitigates OWASP Top 10 API vulnerabilities, and signs downstream service-to-service requests with under 3.5ms proxy latency overhead.

use_cases.title: High-Security Open Banking API Gateway Authorization
use_cases.first_sentence: Financial microservices serving third-party fintech applications must validate asymmetric client signatures without exposing sensitive internal network endpoints.
use_cases.second_sentence: The Node.js gateway validates incoming RS256 JWT tokens against published JWKS key endpoints and forwards authenticated requests to internal banking services.

use_cases.title: Instantaneous Compromised Session Revocation for Enterprise SSO
use_cases.first_sentence: When a security incident detects compromised user credentials, security operations teams must invalidate active sessions immediately across all edge nodes.
use_cases.second_sentence: The gateway blacklists revoked token IDs in a Redis Bloom filter within 25ms, instantly rejecting subsequent requests without waiting for JWT TTL expiry.

use_cases.title: Edge Microservice Layer 7 Threat Filtering & Fingerprint Verification
use_cases.first_sentence: Public customer portals are targeted by automated credential stuffing bots replaying captured authorization tokens from novel IP addresses.
use_cases.second_sentence: The gateway computes SHA-256 client device fingerprints (User-Agent, TLS ciphers, IP subnets) and terminates replayed requests with mismatched fingerprints.

hard_parts: Implementing automated RS256 asymmetric keypair rotation with zero-downtime JWKS cache invalidation across distributed edge gateway instances
Designing an in-memory Redis Bloom filter token revocation registry supporting sub-millisecond membership checks and 0 false negatives

Achieving sub-3.5ms proxy latency overhead while executing cryptographic signature verification and rate limiting under 2,000 RPS

architecture.data_flow: An external client issues an HTTPS request with an Authorization Bearer JWT; the Express gateway extracts the token header to locate the `kid` (key ID); the JWT engine validates the RS256 signature against local cached JWKS public keys; the token's `jti` (JWT ID) is checked against the Redis Bloom filter in < 1ms; if found in the blacklist, the request is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized; the security middleware computes the client device fingerprint and compares it to claims embedded in the token; if valid, the request is proxied to the backend microservice with downstream identity headers; Prometheus tracks latency and rejection counts.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Cryptographic RS256 asymmetric signature verification combined with Redis Bloom filter membership checks.

riskiest_component.name: False Positives in Bloom Filter Token Revocation causing Legitimate User Logouts
riskiest_component.mitigation: Size Bloom filter capacity with 0.001 error probability and perform secondary exact Redis SET check on positive matches.
riskiest_component.fallback: Secondary exact key check eliminating false positives before rejecting requests.

worksheet.q2: Target users: security software engineers, API gateway platform developers, and backend infrastructure engineers.
